 Winter Utility Aid: How Meridian Families Can Get LIHEAP Assistance
 By 
 Veronica Adams 
 Published 
 October 30, 2026 
 10:45 am 
 MERIDIAN, Miss. (Queen City Newsfeed)— With cooler weather approaching and heating demands on the rise, low-income households across Lauderdale County and East Mississippi can receive financial relief through the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program.
 The federally funded program, administered by the Mississippi Department of Human Services, provides financial aid to qualifying families to offset home heating and cooling costs, handle emergency disconnects, and fund weatherization repairs across all 82 counties in Mississippi.
 What the Program Covers
 Assistance under the program is broken into three key service areas:
 Home Energy Bills: Direct payments made on behalf of approved applicants to approved energy providers, covering electricity, natural gas, wood, liquid propane, or butane gas.
 Energy Crisis Intervention Program: Emergency relief for households facing imminent service shutoffs or utility disconnections, often processed within 48 hours.
 Weatherization and Repair: Energy-efficiency upgrades, insulation improvements, and repair or replacement of faulty heaters, furnaces, or HVAC systems.
 The program prioritizes vulnerable households, specifically families with children age 5 or younger, individuals with disabilities, and senior citizens.
 Who Qualifies
 Eligibility is primarily based on household size and income limits. Applicants must meet the following criteria:
 Income Limits: Total household gross income must fall at or below 60% of Mississippi’s median income, or up to 200% of federal poverty guidelines for specialized weatherization assistance.
 Residency: Applicants must be Mississippi residents age 18 or older, or legally emancipated minors.
 Utility Responsibility: Utility accounts must typically be in the name of the household head or spouse. Renters whose utilities are included in their lease can apply with proper landlord documentation or lease verification.
 How to Apply in Lauderdale County
 Applying is a multi-step process that begins online before routing to local administrators:
 Submit an Initial Pre-Application: Residents can begin the process online through the state’s AccessMS portal or the Virtual ROMA pre-application portal.
 Local Agency Review: Applications are routed to the Multi-County Community Service Agency, the designated community action agency serving Lauderdale and surrounding East Mississippi counties. Case managers will contact applicants to schedule an intake interview.
 Required Documentation: Applicants must provide government-issued photo identification for all adults in the home, proof of income covering the last 30 days (such as pay stubs, Social Security award letters, or tax forms), copies of recent utility bills, and residency verification.
 Direct Provider Credit: Once an application is approved, funds do not go directly to the applicant; payments are credited directly to the resident’s utility provider.
 Residents in Lauderdale County needing assistance with the pre-application process or facing an immediate utility shutoff can contact the Multi-County Community Service Agency central office in Meridian at 601-483-4838, or visit the MDHS portal at access.ms.gov.
 Social Media / App Push Blurb:
 Winter heating aid is opening up for East Mississippi families. Here is how Lauderdale County residents can qualify and apply for state utility bill assistance through LIHEAP.
